sections.overview: The Bar-tailed Godwit is an Arctic-breeding shorebird that migrates between northern breeding grounds and coastal wintering areas.
sections.identification: Its shorter legs, slightly upturned bill and lack of white wing-bars in flight distinguish it from the Black-tailed Godwit.
sections.habitat: Outside the breeding season it is mainly coastal, using intertidal mudflats and sandy-muddy shores. It breeds in open Arctic tundra.
sections.diet: It probes soft sediment for invertebrates, including marine worms and small crustaceans; the mix of prey varies among feeding sites.
sections.behavior: Some individuals make exceptionally long non-stop migratory flights, while others use coastal stopovers; routes and timing differ among populations and subspecies.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground in treeless tundra. A clutch is usually four eggs, incubated by both sexes.
sections.ecology: Its close congener is the Black-tailed Godwit (*Limosa limosa*); see that profile for the reciprocal comparison.
sections.conservation: The BTO reports a global IUCN category of Near Threatened; its page also distinguishes this from UK and European assessments, which use different scales and contexts.
